{{Quote|The Aiwha of our world hunt in pods to bring down much larger prey.|[[Taun We/Legends|Taun We]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
'''Aiwha''' {{Pronounced|Äē'-wä}}<ref name="NEGAS" /> were flying cetacean creatures that lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planets]] [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] and [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. They could use their wing-fins to either propel themselves through water or to soar through the skies. [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]] were derogatorily referred to as "aiwha-bait" by various clones of [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], bred at a cloning facility on the planet.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|We've got to stop meeting like this, my friend.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to an aiwha after falling on it for a second time|<ref name="ARC Troopers">{{TCW|ARC Troopers (episode)}}</ref>}}
Majestic [[Cetacean/Legends|cetaceans]] that could take to the air,<ref name=":0">{{DB|creature|aiwha|aiwha}}</ref> aiwhas could be found in the churning oceans of the planet [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], where they had been domesticated as mounts by the native [[Kaminoan/Legends|Kaminoans]]. The creatures were strong swimmers, able to launch themselves from the cresting waves and then continue their momentum in flight.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref>

[[File:Aiwhas-ARCT.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Aiwhas swimming beneath the surface of Kamino's oceans]]
Aiwhas and similar creatures could be found on several worlds, including the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name=":0" /> There, they lived in medium-size "[[Pod (social group)|pods]]," feeding on surface-dwelling [[Krill (creature)/Legends|krill]] and the fish (like [[Mee/Legends|daggerts]] and [[Ray/Legends|rays]])<ref name=":1">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> found in the huge Naboo lakes. Like other [[Cetacean/Legends|cetaceans]],<ref name=":0" /> aiwhas filtered food through the sieve-plates in their baleen. The [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] of Naboo had domesticated aiwhas to accept mounts and provide airborne transportation. Gungans also used the aiwhas as war mounts, using them as reconnaissance and bombers. Aiwhas employed a water-vascular system that allowed them to control their relative density. When they needed to swim underwater, their spongy tissues absorbed water. When flight was required, they expelled this water and shed it to lighten themselves.<ref name=":1" />

While some believed the aiwhas on Kamino to have been imported from Naboo, others speculated that this particular breed was entirely the result of [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] technology.<ref name=":0" />

Aiwhas were sold by the [[Rothana Heavy Engineering/Legends|Rothana Heavy Engineering]] company to be used as mounts for [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] troops, who used them on worlds that had a breathable atmosphere, and could be used for performing reconnaissance over 5,000 meters overhead, or to traverse between two Imperial outposts without any concern for the trail or terrain. A standard animal cost 45000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] at a starting price, and larger, cargo-hauling breeds were available under the premium pricing model.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Titavian2-woswfg.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Gugans riding aiwhas.]]
The word "aiwha" is a deliberate corruption of "air whale." They are also called Air Whales in the ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption]]'' game manual.<ref name="Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion: Prima Official Game Guide">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War: Forces of Corruption Expansion'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

Aiwhas existed, in one form or another, for over twenty years before being incorporated into a ''Star Wars'' movie. Concept illustrator [[Ralph McQuarrie]] drew flying [[Wikipedia:whale|whales]] to populate [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']], but they were a casualty of budget and effects limitations. They resurfaced as transports on the planet [[Sicemon]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], but were ultimately replaced with the more practical sail barge and skiffs when the world didn't appear in the final film. For [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']], the aiwhas returned as Gungan mounts, but were again dropped from the finished film. For [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], they were to be possible mounts for the Geonosians before finally finding a home on Kamino.<ref name=":0" />

The aiwha bears a striking similarity to the [[Thranta/Legends|thrantas]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], and the [[Neebray/Legends|neebray]] of [[Rugosa/Legends|Rugosa]] and the [[Balmorra Run/Legends|Balmorra Run]], but no [[in-universe]] relation has been documented between any of the three species.
